literature.title: Detection and Validation of Hidden Subgroup Disparities in Clinical AI
literature.what_it_means: Addresses safety of clinical ML via subgroup discovery, relevant to Waymark's AI monitoring (Signal, Compass, Anchor). However, chest X-ray imaging is not Waymark's core domain; transfer to text-based care coordination and risk prediction models unclear. Preprint, unvalidated on Medicaid workflows.

literature.title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System
literature.what_it_means: ALLMTS addresses LLM safety and omission errors—core Waymark interests. Synthetic validation only; real clinical deployment safety and Medicaid applicability untested. Relevant to Anchor's verification layer.

literature.title: Long-term retention and associated factors among volunteer community health workers in southwestern Uganda: a 17-to-21-year retrospective cohort study
literature.what_it_means: CHW retention factors are operationally relevant to Waymark, but Uganda's volunteer, low-resource model differs fundamentally from US paid CHW teams in capitated Medicaid. Transfer requires explicit assumption testing.

literature.title: Community Health Worker Coaching, Food Insecurity, and Physical Activity in the Healthy Food First Trial: A Causal Mediation and Longitudinal Analysis
literature.what_it_means: This secondary analysis of a randomized trial found no clear effect on physical activity or evidence of mediation through food insecurity; estimates were imprecise. Food insecurity is relevant to Waymark's social-needs work, but transfer to Medicaid managed care depends on comparability with food-insecure adults with hypertension recruited in North Carolina.

literature.title: GLLaucoMed: A Secure Large Language Model–Powered Agentic Workflow for Automated Medication Extraction from Free-Text Glaucoma Clinical Notes
literature.what_it_means: Paper addresses NLP of clinical notes and LLM-based information extraction relevant to Waymark's pharmacy program and AI safety interests. However, glaucoma-specific ophthalmology notes may not transfer to primary-care or chronic-disease populations Waymark serves.

literature.title: Telepharmacy-based mobile health for diabetes care: models, benefits, and barriers-a scoping review
literature.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of 6 telepharmacy studies in non-US, non-Medicaid settings. Evidence is limited, and transfer to US Medicaid managed care is unclear. The abstract describes pharmacist roles, benefits, and barriers but does not report comparative evidence on reach or team workflows.

literature.title: Study protocol for the Healthier Wealthier Families (HWF) cluster randomised controlled trial: testing the effectiveness and cost-benefits of offering financial counselling to families with young children who report financial hardship at well-child health home visits
literature.what_it_means: Tests integration of social-needs screening (financial hardship) into home visiting. Australian public well-child system differs from US Medicaid managed care; no direct US Medicaid population or payer context.

literature.title: Moral distress in pediatric complex care coordinators: a reflexive thematic analysis
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study of moral distress, its influencing factors and its impacts among care coordinators at a tertiary pediatric hospital. Transferability to adult Medicaid community-based care coordinators is uncertain; the study setting differs from Waymark's capitated community care.

literature.title: Variation in 90‐day substance use disorder‐related acute care events across United States opioid treatment programs: A Medicaid claims analysis
literature.what_it_means: Identifies reliable OTP-level performance variation on a preventable outcome; relevant to Waymark's behavioral-health and care-coordination programs. Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; no intervention tested.

literature.title: State Design and Use of Medicaid 1915(c) Waivers and Related Benefits to Provide Home‐ and Community‐Based Services to Aging and Disabled Adults: The Medicaid HCBS Waiver Atlas
literature.what_it_means: Develops infrastructure (dataset) for rigorous Medicaid program evaluation via policy variation. Directly relevant to Waymark's interest in causal methods with observational data. However, no outcomes or program effects demonstrated yet.

literature.title: How Common Are Social Determinants of Health? A Comparison of National Estimates and Health System-Reported Prevalence
literature.what_it_means: Addresses SDOH screening accuracy, relevant to Waymark's social-needs program. However, setting is regional integrated system with unknown insurance mix; no Medicaid-specific data. No causal or programmatic evidence.

literature.title: Effectiveness of Digital Commitment Devices in Improving Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Adults with Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
literature.what_it_means: Digital commitments could fit Waymark's behavioral engagement, including COMPASS texts. Adults with cardiometabolic risk plausibly overlap with Waymark's Medicaid population. But the abstract does not establish Medicaid-specific effectiveness, sustained benefits beyond 12 months, or applicability to Waymark's team-based care.

literature.title: Administrative Workload and Associated Distress in Individuals Undergoing Cancer Therapy
literature.what_it_means: In this observational cohort of people receiving cancer treatment, administrative tasks were associated with distress, and unreliable transportation was associated with more time spent on those tasks. Findings could inform care-coordination triage, but applicability to Waymark's Medicaid members is uncertain; payer mix was not reported.

literature.title: From clinician review to measurable human oversight of AI-drafted paediatric discharge documents
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses clinician oversight of AI outputs, relevant to Anchor's error-detection design. However, pediatric ED discharge letters differ structurally and contextually from Waymark's SMS and care-coordination workflows.

literature.title: Human oversight of erroneous clinical AI and decision support a systematic review and meta analysis
literature.what_it_means: Anchor is a physician-facing verification layer checking AI outputs for omissions and errors. This systematic review directly evaluates whether clinician oversight catches AI errors—core to Anchor's design rationale and safety evaluation.

literature.title: Developing an operational framework for hybrid cardiac rehabilitation in a safety-net healthcare system
literature.what_it_means: Describes operational framework for hybrid care addressing access barriers (distance, transport) relevant to Waymark's population. No outcome data, no causal claims. Transferable logic but narrow disease focus.

literature.title: Alcohol use screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment cascade of care in the USA: Variation by alcohol use and socio‐demographic characteristics
literature.what_it_means: Documents disparities in SBIRT implementation that could inform Waymark's behavioral-health and care-coordination work with Medicaid populations. However, it is descriptive of screening rates, not a test of an intervention or model to adopt.

literature.title: Technology-based structural racism and telehealth video usage among primary care patients
literature.what_it_means: Identifies telehealth modality disparities by race. Relevant if Waymark uses video for behavioral health or remote care coordination, but this study is observational health equity documentation, not an intervention or predictive model.

literature.title: Social Determinants of Health and Incident Type 2 Diabetes Risk: Real-World Evidence From the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Learning Health System Registry
literature.what_it_means: Study validates that aggregated SDoH predicts diabetes incidence in real-world EMR data—relevant to Waymark's social-needs screening and identification. However, no intervention tested; unclear if actionable for whom-to-reach algorithms or what-to-do decisions.

literature.title: The Benefits and Costs of Treating Obesity Among Adults in the Medicaid Program
literature.what_it_means: Models social ROI from obesity treatment in Medicaid, with 5.9M potential referrals among adults with obesity lacking qualifying obesity-related complications. Relevant to referral planning, but not an operational targeting tool. Initiation and continuation rates are modeled; how well they reflect local adherence, retention and care-team capacity remains uncertain.

literature.title: Development of a large language model clinical variable extraction pipeline for the study of lymphedema
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses NLP of care notes and LLM safety (omission-error evaluation). Validates extraction pipeline accuracy, which is relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests. However, lymphedema is a narrow disease; generalization to Waymark's broad population and note types unclear.

literature.title: Numeric versus embedding pipelines for optimized clinical risk prediction
literature.what_it_means: Addresses model transparency and failure modes relevant to Waymark's Signal product. However, ICU acute mortality/readmission tasks differ substantially from community-based chronic disease and social-needs navigation for Medicaid members.

literature.title: Initiatives to Prevent Fatal Drug Overdose Mortality After Incarceration
literature.what_it_means: Commentary synthesizing evidence for policy levers (Medicaid reentry waivers, carceral recovery programs, harm-reduction hubs) relevant to Waymark's justice-involved members. No new empirical findings; unclear which specific initiatives drive outcomes.

literature.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Community-Based, Family Network Heart Health Intervention - the SERVE OC Trial: Design, Rationale and Baseline Findings
literature.venue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
literature.what_it_means: This medRxiv preprint describes a family-centered CHW trial with documented social-needs burden. CHW delivery overlaps with Waymark's approach, but transfer from Latino and Vietnamese families in California to Medicaid managed care needs justification. Only design and baseline findings are reported; cardiovascular and blood pressure outcomes are pending.

literature.title: Impact of clinical pharmacist interventions in psychiatric hospitals on clinical and medication-related outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
literature.what_it_means: Waymark's pharmacist program targets outpatient Medicaid members with chronic disease and serious mental illness, not inpatient psychiatric hospitals. Setting and population differ substantially; generalization to community-based care is uncertain.

literature.title: Association of Multidisciplinary Care Team Engagement With Hemoglobin A1c Among Medicaid Enrollees With Diabetes: A Doubly Robust Machine Learning Analysis
literature.what_it_means: In a Virginia Medicaid managed-care cohort, care-team engagement was associated with lower HbA1c, with larger estimated benefits at higher baseline HbA1c. Sensitivity estimates had the same direction, but the single-value analysis included no effect. Findings could inform Waymark outreach and Signal hypotheses; targeting performance remains untested.

literature.title: Drug interactions in rheumatoid arthritis: a disparity between electronic database prediction and real-world co-prescription with different large language models
literature.what_it_means: Evaluates LLM agreement with expert drug-interaction judgments—relevant to Waymark medication review, but not direct evidence of safety. RA population is narrow; generalization to Medicaid managed-care polypharmacy is unclear. No causal design or population-health outcome.

literature.title: Strengthening Real‐World Evidence: Recognizing and Overcoming Methodological Pitfalls in Observational Health Data
literature.what_it_means: Addresses methodological rigor for observational real-world evidence, relevant to Waymark's causal evaluation interests. Reviews approaches including target-trial emulation and inverse probability of sampling weighting that could inform claims-based Medicaid analyses.

literature.title: Precision targeting using machine learning to optimize medication therapy management delivery in value-based care: A quasi-experimental study using real-world evidence
literature.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
literature.what_it_means: Waymark's pharmacists provide similar medication review. ML targeting was associated with higher consultation acceptance in a propensity-matched historical comparison. This may inform whom Signal helps teams reach, but engagement targeting differs from rising-risk prediction. Applicability to Medicaid and fit with Waymark's evaluation requirements need assessment.

literature.title: Trends in hepatitis C treatment initiation alongside changes in Medicaid policy requirements: Wisconsin, January 2015-December 2022
literature.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
literature.what_it_means: In Wisconsin Medicaid, removing hepatitis C treatment restrictions was associated with higher treatment initiation, though uptake peaked at only 23%. Relevant to Waymark's coordination and pharmacy work, but this observational study focuses on one disease and policy levers outside Waymark's control.

literature.title: Mapping cardiometabolic risk in Cleveland's urban environment: A participatory systems analysis of place-based drivers and the role of Community Health Workers
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative systems mapping identifies CHW capacity constraints and structural barriers relevant to Waymark's model. This study did not test whether proposed interventions improve outcomes. Its findings may inform program design and place-based outreach priorities, but do not establish causal effects or validate individual targeting.

literature.title: Hybrid human-digital motivational incentive intervention protocol for smoking cessation among perinatal Medicaid patients
literature.what_it_means: Protocol paper describing a single-arm feasibility/acceptability study with no control group or causal evidence. Targets perinatal Medicaid population directly, but provides no efficacy data yet to inform Waymark operations or reach decisions.

literature.title: Associations of Health Insurance with Guideline-Concordant Treatment and Overall Survival Among Women with Breast Cancer
literature.what_it_means: Cohort study of cancer treatment disparities by insurance type. Shows Medicaid patients receive less guideline-concordant care and worse survival. Does not directly address Waymark's interventions (CHW outreach, care coordination, social needs navigation) or mechanisms to close these gaps.

literature.title: A comparison of health care utilization among insured working-age adults in the state of Virginia, U.S. by long COVID and disabling condition status in 2022
literature.what_it_means: Identifies high-utilization subpopulation (PDC+LCOVID) that Waymark might target. Cross-sectional design cannot establish causation or validate predictive ranking. Virginia setting and mixed-payer data partially align but lack Medicaid-specific prevalence and risk stratification.

literature.title: Increase in Methadone Treatment Episodes With Co-occurring Mental Health Disorders between 2013 and 2023
literature.what_it_means: Among selected methadone treatment episodes with psychiatric comorbidity, clients were older, stimulant co-use and homelessness were more common, and Medicaid payment increased. These descriptive comparisons suggest possible needs for integrated care and housing support relevant to Waymark members. The study does not test an intervention or evaluation method.

literature.title: Integrating Scalability and Equity into Hypertension Remote Patient Monitoring Program Design
literature.what_it_means: Reviews scalable, equitable hypertension RPM, including devices, team-based care, outreach, and language and social barriers relevant to Waymark's Medicaid population. Offers implementation lessons for care teams, but does not directly evaluate SMS navigation or risk prediction.

literature.title: Evaluation of a pharmacist-led pharmacogenomic service and provider acceptance at VA Puget Sound
literature.what_it_means: Pharmacist intervention in Medicaid could improve medication safety, but VA population differs from Medicaid managed care. No control group, short timeframe, no clinical outcomes measured.

literature.title: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist’s framework
literature.what_it_means: Describes pharmacist-led medication review framework for older diabetics. Waymark employs clinical pharmacists, but paper provides guidance without empirical validation in Medicaid populations or Waymark-specific outcomes.

literature.title: Race- and Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in Diagnosis and Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation
literature.what_it_means: Addresses underdiagnosis of AF in marginalized populations, relevant to risk prediction equity. However, uses Medicare Advantage/commercial claims, not Medicaid managed care, limiting direct transferability.

literature.title: Wireless Home Blood Pressure Monitoring With Health Coaching for Hypertension Management at a Federally Qualified Health Center: Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility and Acceptability Study
literature.what_it_means: FQHC care could inform Waymark's Medicaid workflows. Monitoring plus coaching may be relevant to care teams. This pilot was underpowered for efficacy; 63% of recruits were analyzed, but randomized-arm counts were unavailable, limiting assessment of attrition. No statistically significant between-arm BP-control difference was found; this does not establish equivalence.

literature.title: Healthcare spending associated with major depressive disorder among U.S. adults
literature.what_it_means: Establishes MDD burden in Medicaid population but provides no intervention evidence or actionable targeting strategy. Descriptive epidemiology only; does not change whom Waymark reaches or what teams do.

literature.title: Emergency department use disparities in schizophrenia: Mediating role of antipsychotic availability and administration
literature.what_it_means: In Medicaid adults with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, claims-based antipsychotic coverage statistically mediated part of the racial difference in ED use. Mediation was not significant for first-generation or long-acting injectable users. Relevant to pharmacy and care-coordination teams, but this observational study did not test whether improving coverage reduces disparities.

literature.title: Benchmarking large language models for HIV medical decision support
literature.what_it_means: Benchmarking study of LLM safety and accuracy in HIV care decision support. Relevant to Waymark's interest in LLM safety and omission-error evaluation, but domain-specific (HIV) and does not directly evaluate a population-health intervention or Medicaid care model.

literature.title: Predictors of Newly Prescribed Medications for Alcohol Use Disorder Among Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study
literature.what_it_means: Identifies modifiable hospitalization factors (care mgmt consult, service structure) linked to MAUD initiation. Could inform whom to reach post-discharge and care-coordination touchpoints, but cohort is hospitalized patients at academic center; generalizability to Medicaid managed-care member population unclear.

literature.title: Evaluating the impact of a multi-year produce prescription program on fruit and vegetable intake, and food security in south central New York
literature.venue: The international journal of behavioral nutrition and physical activity
literature.what_it_means: Addresses food insecurity, a core Waymark social need. Cohort design with matched samples per year but no control group limits causal inference. Setting is US Medicaid-eligible population. Results modest on health outcomes.

literature.title: Comparing different forms of structured follow-up support in the treatment of multiple health risks for chronic disease: a randomized controlled trial protocol
literature.what_it_means: The trial tests CHW-delivered reminders and automated messaging for multi-risk behavior change in primary care. Design and population differ from Waymark's capitated, high-need Medicaid model; cancer-risk focus is narrow. Relevance depends on trial results and explicit transferability analysis.

literature.title: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations
literature.what_it_means: Addresses representation sufficiency in doubly robust causal estimation from multimodal data—directly relevant to Waymark's causal evaluation methods and AI safety concerns. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. No empirical application to health-services outcomes.

literature.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
literature.what_it_means: Addresses AI safety and omission-error evaluation, areas Waymark cares about. But privacy-risk screening is upstream of model use; unclear how identifying vulnerable records changes operations, reach, or team actions.

literature.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
literature.what_it_means: This unreviewed preprint offers evaluation ideas relevant to Compass SMS safety. Its LMIC WhatsApp context differs from US Medicaid SMS. The abstract reports no US data or comparison of evaluation methods' predictive validity.

literature.title: Local Discrimination of Binary Classifiers via Localized AUC Functional
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint proposing localized AUC to identify patient subgroups where prediction models perform poorly. The abstract reports real-world and simulation testing but gives no quantitative results or specific population, payer, or care-setting details. Applicability to Medicaid care remains unclear.

literature.title: Causal inference in staggered adoption panels: The correct comparison set depends on your intervention
literature.what_it_means: Waymark explicitly uses staggered difference-in-differences for causal evaluation with operational variation. This methodological paper clarifies which comparison sets answer which counterfactual questions—critical for designing falsifiable tests.

literature.title: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint presents an evaluation framework separating omissions from fabrications, potentially useful for Waymark's Anchor product. Its oncology abstraction results from Singapore do not establish applicability to Medicaid managed care or effects on care delivery, member reach, or program evaluation.

literature.title: Community Health Worker Density and Child Immunisation Coverage in Nigeria: A Target-Trial Emulation of Health System Decentralisation Effects
literature.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
literature.what_it_means: Paper demonstrates causal design feasibility for CHW interventions using quasi-random variation, aligned with Waymark's methodologic interests. However, Nigeria's public-sector immunization context transfers poorly to US Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: LINGUISTIC OPTIMIZATION OF PATIENT-FACING DRUG DELIVERY INFORMATION USING GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: A READABILITY, TERMINOLOGY AND CONTENT-FIDELITY STUDY
literature.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
literature.what_it_means: Addresses AI-assisted patient communication in pharmacy context, relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacist program and COMPASS safety. However, document-level study on general drug materials; no evidence from actual Medicaid member interactions or care workflows.

literature.title: R-GCRED: a retrieval-grounded and calibrated risk estimation for depression prediction and screening recommendation framework
literature.what_it_means: Addresses AI safety (calibration, evidence grounding, uncertainty) relevant to Waymark's LLM products. But evaluated only on research benchmarks, not prospective clinical validation or real Medicaid workflows.

literature.title: Tenant Right-to-Counsel and Emergency Department Use in Low-Income and Uninsured Populations
literature.what_it_means: Uses a staggered natural experiment and difference-in-differences to study eviction prevention. There was no overall association with ED use. Lower use was associated with the earliest rollout phase; the estimate for children was uncertain. Higher mental-health and substance-use ED use also warrants caution before operationalizing.

literature.title: Are Increased Engagements With Recovery Support Services Associated With Reductions in Medicaid Billing Charges and Reimbursements?
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant population and payer. However, observational study without causal design; cannot rule out confounding (sicker patients may seek more support). Waymark uses quasi-random variation; this study does not.

literature.title: Assisting Screening of Adolescent Depression With Large Language Models as Symptom Detectors: Algorithm Development and Validation
literature.what_it_means: NLP method for depression screening in adolescent EHR notes could improve behavioral health identification and signal design. However, Waymark serves mostly adult Medicaid; pediatric applicability and real-world deployment validation remain unclear.

literature.title: Development and Validation of the Large Language Model Privacy Concern Assessment Questionnaire: Psychometric Evaluation Study on a Brief Instrument for Assessing User Privacy Concerns With Large Language Model Applications
literature.what_it_means: Psychometric instrument development for LLM privacy concerns is relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests, but the study population (mostly college-educated, young, White, general public) does not represent Medicaid members or clinical workflows.

literature.title: Effect of a Multilevel Intervention on Racial Disparities in Medication Adherence: An Analysis of the Rich Life Project
literature.what_it_means: Pragmatic RCT of team-based care in primary care, relevant to Waymark's care-coordination and pharmacy work. However, setting appears to be commercial/mixed payer primary care practices, not Medicaid managed care. No social-needs assessment or CHW component. Null finding on disparity reduction limits actionability.

literature.title: Association of a Chronic Care Management Model with Health Care Costs and Utilization
literature.what_it_means: Direct operational parallel: multidisciplinary team (RN, pharmacy, BH, CHW) reduces acute utilization in high-risk Medicaid population. Propensity-score matching addresses selection bias. Maryland's Medicaid managed-care structure transfers to Waymark's states.

literature.title: Receipt of needed care coordination and emergency department utilization among US children with chronic physical pain: a pooled analysis of the 2022–2024 National Survey of Children's Health
literature.what_it_means: Cross-sectional findings cannot establish causation or temporal ordering; unmeasured need severity may confound the association. Receipt of needed care coordination was associated with lower ED use among children with chronic pain. Prospective causal evaluation is needed before using this finding to guide Waymark operations.

literature.title: Scaling Therapy Supervision: Assessing Psychotherapy Fidelity Using Large Language Models
literature.what_it_means: LLM-based fidelity feedback could improve Waymark therapist supervision and self-learning. However, preprint lacks peer review, sample sizes unreported, and generalization to Medicaid populations unstated. RCT validation on CBT/non-CBT distinction does not measure patient outcomes or feedback utility at scale.

literature.title: Estimand frameworks for causal inference in clinical research and regulatory decision making
literature.what_it_means: Methodological framework relevant to Waymark's stated interest in causal evaluation and target-trial emulation. However, it is a conceptual paper without empirical validation in Waymark's population or programs.

literature.title: From Scores to Safe Sets: Exact Safety--Constrained Decoding for Medication Recommendation
literature.what_it_means: Addresses medication safety optimization, relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacist program. However, uses fixed pretrained scores on historical EHR data without validation on live Medicaid populations or prospective safety outcomes.

literature.title: BRIDGE: An Acceptance Gate to Block False Improvements in Model Updates, with a Retrospective Clinical Evaluation
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint explores rejecting model updates whose validation gains fail on new data. Cross-fitting and bootstrap-bound thresholds could inform Signal and Anchor deployment gates. Clinical testing was retrospective; prospective performance in US Medicaid remains unestablished.

literature.title: Generative AI in clinical practice: how should rheumatologists evaluate and monitor emerging tools?
literature.what_it_means: Proposes AI evaluation framework relevant to Waymark's anchor product (verification layer for AI outputs). Addresses hallucinations, automation bias, and documentation errors. However, rheumatology-specific; no Medicaid or community health worker data; no empirical validation of framework.

literature.title: Access to prescription medication labels in Spanish from community pharmacies
literature.what_it_means: Small qualitative study identifies a modifiable pharmacy barrier (label language) affecting a Medicaid-relevant population. Could inform pharmacist workflows, but study lacks causal evidence and clinical outcomes.

literature.title: Health Data Utilities as Essential Public Infrastructure: A Cooperative Federalism Architecture
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Waymark's risk identification and eligibility workflows: proposes state health data utilities that combine clinical, claims, and social-service data. This is a policy architecture, not an empirical demonstration of improved outcomes.

literature.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's safety evaluation needs and LLM hallucination mitigation. However, abstract reports only benchmarked tasks, not real clinical workflows, member outcomes, or Medicaid settings. Transferability to production requires validation on actual care notes and clinical decisions.

literature.title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
literature.what_it_means: CS1 addresses clinical NLP and population screening relevant to Waymark's Signal (identification) and LLM-safety interests. However, it is trained on inpatient hospital records, not Medicaid outpatient populations, and the paper does not validate on Medicaid data or demonstrate transferability.

literature.title: A plug-in estimator of the non-iterative conditional expectation g-formula using long short-term memory models
literature.what_it_means: An unreviewed preprint explores an LSTM-based g-formula estimator for causal inference with time-varying confounding. It offers proof of concept using simulated data resembling an HIV cohort; no real-world evaluation or transfer to Medicaid populations is reported.

literature.title: Doubly Robust Estimation and Inference for Longitudinal Win Probabilities with Ordinal Outcomes in Observational Studies
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint relevant to Waymark's interest in doubly robust estimators and observational evaluation. The application involves hospitalized adults with acute respiratory illness; Medicaid applicability is not established. Simulations show benefits, but the abstract does not establish superiority over simpler alternatives in realistic settings.

literature.title: When Do Humans and Machines Truly Complement Each Other? Formal Conditions and Empirical Evidence for Human-AI Synergy
literature.what_it_means: Formal framework on human-AI complementarity directly relevant to Anchor (verification layer checking AI outputs). Preprint with seven clinical case studies; setting and population unspecified. No Medicaid/managed-care specificity.

literature.title: Interpretable subgroup identification across survival and generalized-linear outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on subgroup identification in trials. Signal relies on whom-to-reach predictions, but this targets trial post-hoc subgroup mining, not prospective targeting in observational settings Waymark uses.

literature.title: The crystal ball problem: why prediction models are not guaranteed to improve health outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses the gap between prediction and outcome improvement—core to Signal's next-best-action logic. Argues for causal rather than accuracy-only validation, aligned with Waymark's methods interest. Case study is ICU-specific; transferability to community Medicaid care coordination unclear.

literature.title: Expertise modulates automation bias and sentinel behavior in human–AI collaborative diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's verification-layer design and LLM-safety evaluation. However, neonatal radiology diagnosis is far from Waymark's population (adult/pediatric Medicaid with social needs, chronic disease, SMI) and care setting (community-based navigation vs. hospital emergency diagnosis).

literature.title: A Conversation Tool to Enhance Care for People With Type 2 Diabetes
literature.what_it_means: Null RCT of a shared-decision-making tool in a safety-net primary care setting with Medicaid-eligible patients. Relevant to Waymark's care-coordination and behavioral-health work but shows no benefit on fit-of-care or clinical outcomes. Design is sound but underpowered and single-center.

literature.title: Community health worker certification as a pathway to workforce development and career advancement: a qualitative study
literature.what_it_means: Addresses CHW workforce retention and career development, which affect Waymark's ability to sustain local teams. Qualitative evidence on certification's role in retention is relevant but does not measure impact on member outcomes or care delivery.

literature.title: Synthetic gatekeeping in health chatbots: configured answer systems as the unit of AI evaluation and governance for medical information
literature.what_it_means: Theoretical framework for evaluating configured AI systems, not empirical evidence. Addresses AI safety/governance but in chatbots, not Waymark's care-coordination context. No Medicaid population or outcomes.

literature.title: Inhaled treatment adherence patterns and related barriers across three monthly follow-up waves among patients with cough variant asthma: a clinical natural language processing study
literature.what_it_means: NLP extraction of adherence barriers from clinical notes is methodologically relevant to Waymark's care-note NLP work and pharmacy program. However, this single-center adult CVA cohort with telephone follow-up differs from Waymark's Medicaid managed-care population with complex social needs, limiting direct transfer.

literature.title: Impact of Fixed-Dose Combination Therapies on Cardiovascular Mortality and Major Cardiovascular Events
literature.what_it_means: Polypharmacy simplification could support Waymark's pharmacy program for high-risk Medicaid members. However, review focuses on clinical outcomes in cardiovascular populations, not social determinants or integrated care delivery. Transferability to US Medicaid uncertain; most trials conducted outside US.

literature.title: Identifying Social Need Trends Among Emergency Department Super-Users: A Latent Class Analysis
literature.venue: The western journal of emergency medicine
literature.what_it_means: Need-based groups among ED super-users may inform Waymark's social-needs and behavioral-health programs. This population shares features with Waymark's high-utilizer members. The study used chart review and tested no intervention; its cross-sectional design cannot establish causation or show who benefits from which intervention.

literature.title: Agentic artificial intelligence for code status extraction from clinical notes: a cross-model comparison of single agent, reflective agent, and multiagent extractor-reviewer system
literature.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's anchor product (verification layer checking AI outputs for omissions and errors). Suggests single-agent designs may be more efficient than multiagent review. Setting is hospital ICU, not primary Waymark population (community-based Medicaid). No intervention, no outcomes beyond extraction accuracy.

literature.title: Food insecurity in the development of metabolic diseases
literature.what_it_means: Links food insecurity with cardiometabolic risk and names Food as Medicine as a promising intervention class, relevant to Waymark's social-needs screening and community referral. Evidence is mainly associational; the review calls for rigorous evaluation of these interventions.

literature.title: Trust the Edge, Doubt the Arrow: Auditing Validation Signals for Text-Mined Clinical Causal Knowledge Graphs
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint addresses LLM safety and causal-knowledge validation in EHR contexts, aligning with Waymark's interests in NLP of care notes and causal evaluation. It is a methods study, not a Medicaid program or population study. Transfer to care-coordination workflows remains uncertain.

literature.title: Concordance Plausibility Check for Intervention-Conditioned Human Digital Twins
literature.what_it_means: Preprint methodological contribution on assessing the plausibility of causal claims in digital twins. Relevant to Waymark's interest in causal evaluation and LLM/model safety; the supplied abstract reports no empirical demonstration.

literature.title: Nesting or resolution? Facility proxies for variance estimation versus confounding adjustment in claims data without facility identifiers
literature.what_it_means: Addresses methodological challenge (missing facility identifiers in de-identified claims) directly relevant to Waymark's causal evaluation work. Japanese health system structure differs from US Medicaid managed care; transfer depends on whether US claims face similar de-identification constraints.

literature.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Compass (patient-facing AI SMS navigator) safety evaluation. Preprint; evaluation on benchmark, not real deployed systems. Transfer to Medicaid member population unclear.

literature.title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed methods preprint targets generalizing trial treatment effects to broader populations. Waymark's stated evaluation interests focus on observational data. The method is not designed for observational program evaluation; its relevance would depend on having suitable trial and target-population data.

literature.title: Where to weight? Estimating population causal effects with weighted double score matching in complex surveys
literature.what_it_means: Unreviewed arXiv preprint on survey-weighted matching for causal inference. Waymark faces confounding and overlap challenges in observational program evaluation, but the method targets complex surveys. Its usefulness for administrative claims would need evaluation.

literature.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests and Signal's use of LLMs for next-best-action suggestions, but limited to inpatient hospital prediction tasks without Medicaid-managed-care or primary-care population evidence.

literature.title: Incorporating therapist capacity, availability and turnover in trials of therapist-delivered interventions: Non-orthogonal factorial designs
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint proposing randomization strategies for therapist-delivered interventions, evaluated in simulations. It may inform future trials in Waymark's behavioral health program, but applicability to Waymark is untested and it does not directly address observational causal evaluation.

literature.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments
literature.what_it_means: This arXiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed, proposes a doubly robust method for survival treatment effects with time-varying treatments. It aligns with Waymark's interest in causal evaluation of population-health programs. The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and numerical experiments, but no validation in Medicaid or social-needs populations.

literature.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Expanding Housing Access for People Experiencing Homelessness and Opioid Use Disorder in California
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed model projects that expanding Housing First access for unhoused people with OUD in California could be cost-effective. Waymark may reach unhoused Medicaid members with OUD, but the model does not evaluate identification, engagement, or care coordination in managed care.

literature.title: Comorbidity Exposure-Window Definitions and Multidimensional Disparities in Long COVID Risk: Evidence from a U.S. National Cohort (2020-2024)
literature.what_it_means: Non-peer-reviewed cohort preprint examining how EHR comorbidity exposure windows change Long COVID risk estimates, using double/debiased machine learning. Potentially relevant to Waymark's Signal risk models, but the broad adult EHR cohort is not Medicaid-specific, and transfer to capitated care targeting remains uncertain.

literature.title: Key considerations in the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of observational studies in dialysis
literature.venue: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
literature.what_it_means: Methodological review directly applicable to Waymark's stated interest in target-trial emulation for causal evaluation. However, dialysis is a narrow clinical domain; transfer to population-health interventions in Medicaid managed care is not demonstrated.

literature.title: Readmission of children in foster care to psychiatric residential treatment facilities
literature.what_it_means: Identifies high-risk subgroup (foster care youth) with elevated psychiatric residential readmission. Relevant to Waymark's behavioral_health and care_coordination but does not directly evaluate a Waymark-type intervention or suggest actionable next-best actions for care teams.

literature.title: Initial Treatment for Acute Low Back Pain and Risk of Opioid Use Disorder and Overdose
literature.what_it_means: May inform initial acute low back pain referrals and suggest candidate predictors for Signal. The retrospective cohort studied opioid-naive Medicaid adults under age 65 in expansion states. Findings are associations; applicability to Waymark members and value for OUD prediction need local assessment.

literature.title: Propensity Score Methods and Target Trial Emulation in Orthopaedic Surgery: A Practical Guide to Causal Inference from Observational Data
literature.what_it_means: Methodological guidance on causal inference from observational data directly relevant to Waymark's stated interest in target-trial emulation and quasi-experimental designs. Orthopedic setting differs, but principles transfer.

literature.title: Large Language Model–Generated Synthetic Data for Parole and Probation Detection in Clinical Notes: Development and Evaluation Study
literature.what_it_means: NLP detection of parole or probation in notes could support care coordination. Real-world evaluation used VA notes only; usefulness for Medicaid eligibility screening and transfer across documentation practices remain untested.

literature.title: Variation in Medical Ethics Recommendations Across Large Language Models: Case-Based Audit Study
literature.what_it_means: Tests LLM behavior on ethics cases, relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests and Anchor verification layer. But no clinical population, no Medicaid setting, no measurement of downstream clinician or patient impact.

literature.title: “There is a Place for it”: Practitioners’ Perspectives on Situated Ethical Acceptability of AI Technologies for Mental Health Practice (Preprint)
literature.what_it_means: Small qualitative study of practitioner perspectives on AI ethics in mental health. Relevant to Waymark's behavioral health and LLM-safety interests, but focused on practitioner views rather than member outcomes or measured operational changes. Applicability to US Medicaid care is not established.

literature.title: Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios
literature.what_it_means: Tests LLM accuracy on clinical scenarios without real care teams, members, or patient outcomes. Anchor checks AI and clinical outputs for omissions and errors; this benchmark is relevant to LLM safety but doesn't validate Waymark's actual use case or population.

literature.title: Multilevel predictors of stable treatment for opioid use disorder in pregnant individuals enrolled in Medicaid
literature.venue: Journal of substance use and addiction treatment
literature.what_it_means: Identifies actionable contextual and individual barriers to medication adherence in a Medicaid OUD population. Suggests whom to reach (high-vulnerability pregnant people, rural areas with low MOUD access) and what care teams should prioritize (access facilitation, social support).

literature.title: Human-in-the-loop LLM-assisted thematic analysis: A validated, reproducible tutorial for large-scale qualitative research
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM safety and validation rigor relevant to Waymark's AI products (Compass, Signal, Anchor), but demonstration uses Reddit posts, not clinical or care-coordination text. Transfer to Medicaid care notes unclear.

literature.title: “I really can’t imagine anything that could’ve been more easy”: patient perspectives on low-threshold peer-facilitated telemedicine hepatitis C treatment for people who use drugs
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study of peer-facilitated care model for rural PWUD with HCV. Peer support and care coordination resonate with Waymark's CHW/coordinator work, but hepatitis C treatment specificity limits direct applicability. No Medicaid enrollment data reported.

literature.title: Conformal Policy Selection: When to Deploy AI Decisions for Targeted Intervention
literature.what_it_means: Addresses safe deployment of risk-targeting AI and heterogeneous treatment effects—relevant to Signal. Methods preprint, not peer reviewed, with theoretical guarantees and semi-synthetic validation, not real-world deployment evidence yet.

literature.title: DeDiCa: A Scalable Deconfounding Discrete Causal Generative Model
literature.what_it_means: This unreviewed preprint proposes a method for causal inference with hidden confounding that could support Waymark's causal-evaluation interests. The supplied abstract reports no health or Medicaid validation, so transferability remains unclear.

literature.title: Recognizing Study Lineage Is Not Enough: Over-Crediting Same-Trial Evidence in LLM-Based Medical Verification
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed methods preprint examines LLM evidence aggregation, relevant to Anchor's verification layer. It evaluates model behavior using clinical publication families, not patient outcomes. The supplied evidence does not establish validation in payer or clinical workflows; applicability to Medicaid care decisions needs testing.

literature.title: Federated causal inference for effect estimation in healthcare: methods, challenges, and applications
literature.what_it_means: Methods review addresses Waymark's interest in causal evaluation with observational data across distributed settings. But abstract lacks empirical validation in Medicaid managed care; applicability depends on methodological solutions to confounding and heterogeneity.

literature.title: Automated Calculation of the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) Intra-Abdominal Injury Rule from Unstructured Emergency Department Notes Using a Large Language Model
literature.venue: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
literature.what_it_means: One LLM extracted PECARN variables from pediatric ED trauma notes with over 94% accuracy against clinician review. This is relevant to Waymark's NLP and Anchor evaluation interests, but does not establish reliability in Medicaid care notes. Transfer to Waymark's community-based care setting needs testing.

literature.title: Performance Evaluation of the Latest General-Purpose Large Language Models in Medical Reasoning and Clinical Screening Tasks
literature.what_it_means: The study evaluates LLMs on medical exam questions and orthopedic literature screening. It may inform Anchor evaluation, but it does not validate omission-error detection or establish transfer to Medicaid care coordination or member outreach.

literature.title: Lessons From a Quality Improvement Initiative to Address Transportation Barriers in an Urban Primary Care Practice
literature.venue: Journal of primary care & community health
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses unmet social needs (transportation) that Waymark tackles. Workflow integration and rideshare model are plausibly applicable. But n=22 pilot lacks comparison group, causal evidence, or Medicaid-specific validation.

literature.title: Patterns of social determinants of health screening and health-related social needs among patients with newly diagnosed breast cancer in a safety-net system
literature.what_it_means: Documents SDOH screening patterns and reassessment timing among breast cancer patients in a safety-net system. May inform Medicaid social-needs screening, but transferability is uncertain. Descriptive only—no intervention or causal claim tested.

literature.title: Navigating Health Information Sharing to Address Social Needs: Practice, Research, and Policy Recommendations from Hospital-Based Violence Intervention
literature.venue: The Journal of law, medicine & ethics : a journal of the American Society of Law, Medicine & Ethics
literature.what_it_means: Addresses information-sharing barriers relevant to Waymark's social-needs and care-coordination work. However, this is a qualitative policy-practice paper without empirical impact data on outcomes or operations.

literature.title: The Intersection of Place and Need: How Lack of Enrollment Offices Deters Participation in the Safety Net
literature.what_it_means: Addresses structural barriers to safety-net participation using quasi-experimental methods. Relevant to Waymark's re-enrollment (waypoint) and social-needs navigation, but SNAP enrollment differs from Medicaid re-enrollment workflows and member engagement.

literature.title: Hepatitis C screening strategies and linkage-to-care approaches in U.S. emergency departments: A systematic review and meta-analysis
literature.what_it_means: Review compares CHW-led navigation to other linkage strategies for HCV, relevant to Waymark's care-coordination model. However, ED-specific context and outcome focus (HCV cure) differ from Waymark's broader population-health approach. Medicaid fit unclear; payer mix not specified.

literature.title: Automated, Component-Level Assessment of a National Inpatient Diabetes Guideline: Adherence and Its Association with Hospitalization Complications Across Six Hospitals
literature.what_it_means: Inpatient diabetes guideline adherence in Israeli hospitals does not directly transfer to Waymark's outpatient Medicaid population. No Medicaid or US setting. Automation approach and causal methods (IPTW) are methodologically relevant but population/setting mismatch is substantial.

literature.title: Social Needs Z Codes and Subsequent Acute Care Across 21 U.S. Health Systems
literature.what_it_means: Challenges Waymark's assumption that Z codes reliably identify hardship for targeting. Shows documentation varies 1–24% across systems; 46–70% of association is administrative artifact, not hardship signal.

literature.title: Enfermeiro gestor de caso no acompanhamento de utentes crónicos em ambiente hospitalar na transição para a comunidade: scoping review
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of nurse case management for hospital-to-community transitions in chronic disease. Only 10 studies included, mostly non-US settings. Population and payer context differ from US Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Community health workers and promotores de salud: a tiered framework for infectious disease prevention and care among California agricultural workers
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses CHW effectiveness in high-need populations with low healthcare engagement and social barriers. Proposes integrated, tiered CHW model. However, agricultural workers differ from typical Medicaid managed-care populations; Medicaid fit unclear without explicit transfer argument.

literature.title: Improving Continuous Glucose Monitoring Access Among Adults With Type 1 Diabetes in an Urban Safety-Net Hospital
literature.what_it_means: Pharmacy and care-coordination teams could consider CGM education and workflow redesign. This internal safety-net improvement study describes no external comparison group. Participants' insurance coverage and a Medicaid managed-care context are not specified, so transfer to Waymark's population needs assessment.

literature.title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects of a Prescription for Produce Subsidy on Diabetes Care Management
literature.what_it_means: HTE analysis of food subsidy for diabetes is relevant to Waymark's social-needs navigation and screening. Population is food-insecure with chronic disease. Setting is US primary care but not Medicaid-specific; insurance mix unclear. Effect sizes modest.

literature.title: The Cost of Inaction in Treating Obesity in the U.S
literature.what_it_means: Modeling study projecting obesity treatment benefits across populations including Medicaid. Relevant to whom Waymark reaches (adults with obesity, chronic disease) but provides no operational evidence about care-team interventions, product behavior, or program evaluation methods Waymark uses.

literature.title: AI safety is a system property, not a sum of individual defenses
literature.what_it_means: Waymark deploys LLMs (Compass) in clinical contexts with vulnerable populations. Understanding how safety failures compound—especially jailbreaking affecting hallucination and fairness—directly informs safe product design and evaluation of omission errors.

literature.title: Beyond the black box in healthcare operations: a structured literature review and governance framework for explainable AI in clinical process intelligence systems
literature.what_it_means: Framework addresses XAI governance for operational systems (relevant to Waymark's Signal, Compass, Anchor products), but review is descriptive, not empirical. Framework is preliminary and explicitly lacks external validation.

literature.title: Relationship extraction for adverse drug events in clinical notes using large language models: a retrospective cross-sectional study
literature.what_it_means: NLP for ADE extraction could support Waymark pharmacist safety review, but applicability to Medicaid managed care remains unestablished. The study evaluated extraction performance, not whether using the models improves medication safety.

literature.title: Federally Qualified Health center–level characteristics associated with sustaining tobacco screening and treatment in the United States, 2020–2024
literature.what_it_means: Links FQHC patient volume and composition to sustained tobacco screening/treatment performance; these associations may reflect organizational capacity. Relevant to Waymark's Medicaid outreach and care coordination, but the cross-sectional design cannot establish effects of interventions or care-team actions.

literature.title: Association of Visual Impairment With Medication Adherence and Unintentional Nonadherence Behaviors in Older Adults With Chronic Diseases: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study
literature.venue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
literature.what_it_means: Visual impairment was associated with lower adherence, suggesting a potential role for pharmacist screening. Simplification, pill organizers, or audio support could be considered but were not tested. The small, single-center sample of older adults limits US Medicaid transferability; the cross-sectional design cannot establish causation or treatment effects.

literature.title: Enhancing Scientific Validity by Integrating EHR and Claims Data in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative
literature.what_it_means: Methodologically relevant to Waymark's causal evaluation interests (target trial emulation), but population is Medicare-only, not Medicaid. Transfer argument needed.

literature.title: Faster but Not Truer, Part 1: A Systematic Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Health Economics and Outcomes Research
literature.venue: Journal of health economics and outcomes research
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses AI performance measurement gaps and validation failures in causal inference—relevant to Signal and Anchor. But population is HEOR literature, not Medicaid operations. Transferability unclear without Waymark-specific analysis.

literature.title: Real-world evaluation of a multilingual agentic retrieval-augmented clinical AI framework for evidence-grounded medical decision support
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's error-detection mission and AI safety priorities. However, this is a benchmark study of physician-facing AI tools, not a real-world evaluation of patient outcomes or care-team behavior in Medicaid settings.

literature.title: Human-in-the-loop large language model framework for identification of cutaneous immune-related adverse events
literature.what_it_means: Framework demonstrates LLM safety via human-in-the-loop design and NLP for note analysis. Oncology setting does not directly transfer to Waymark's Medicaid population, but error-detection methods may inform Anchor validation logic.

literature.title: A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
literature.what_it_means: Demonstrates scalable validation of LLM-based clinical-note extraction without exhaustive manual annotation. Relevant to Anchor's verification role and Waymark's NLP and AI safety interests, though the abstract does not establish how well the framework detects omissions.

literature.title: Postpartum Maternal Preferences on Health-Related Social Needs Programs in the First 1000 Days
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study of maternal preferences on social needs screening timing and resource navigation. Findings could inform Waymark's social-needs program design and care-coordination workflows, but evidence is descriptive without quantified program impact or causal inference.

literature.title: Large language models as raters of hospital incident reports: a blinded multi-model evaluation of severity under-grading and shared errors
literature.venue: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
literature.what_it_means: Directly tests LLM safety for clinical classification—relevant to Waymark's Anchor product (AI verification layer). However, study uses hospital incident reports, not Waymark's care-note context. Transfer to Medicaid care coordination requires validation.

literature.title: Drug–Drug Interactions vs. Therapeutic Combinations in Patients with Congestive Heart Failure and Diabetes: An Ambispective Real‐World Study
literature.what_it_means: Addresses pharmacist medication review workflow and DDI screening, relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacy program. However, hospitalized setting, small sample, cross-sectional design, and lack of causal inference limit evidence strength. No outcome data on safety or health impact.

literature.title: Target Trial Emulation or Target Trial Approximation?
literature.what_it_means: Addresses target-trial emulation, one of Waymark's stated methods interests. Argues the framework has value but cannot eliminate observational-data limitations. Does not propose new methods or present empirical evidence from Medicaid populations.

literature.title: TrialCalibre1: An Agentic System for Trial Emulation, Benchmarking, and Calibration
literature.what_it_means: TrialCalibre1 addresses Waymark's causal-evaluation interests (target-trial emulation, sensitivity analysis) and AI-safety concerns (protocol review, implementation verification). Preprint; limited validation; design departures and residual imbalance acknowledged.

literature.title: Exploring the impact of GLP-1 analogues and DPP-4 inhibitors on cognitive decline in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes: a competing risks analysis from a real-world cohort
literature.what_it_means: This observational medication-class comparison used marginal structural models and competing-risk analyses. The primary outcome combined cognitive disorders with death; cognitive findings alone were inconclusive. Its older population with type 2 diabetes is narrower than Waymark's Medicaid membership, so relevance to pharmacy practice needs evidence in Waymark's population.

literature.title: Flexible Doubly Robust Proximal Causal Inference for Censored Outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Non-peer-reviewed preprint proposing a causal inference method for right-censored survival outcomes under unmeasured confounding. Methods contribution with benchmark and real-world evaluations. Medicaid fit unclear; no operational trial or US managed-care evaluation reported.

literature.title: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint suggests LLM phenotype extraction could inform Waymark's clinical NLP work. It studies Rett syndrome notes at Texas Children's Hospital; ages and Medicaid coverage are not reported. Transferability to Waymark's broader chronic-disease and social-needs work, and usefulness for omission-error detection, remain unclear.

literature.title: Difference-in-Differences for Heterogeneous Effects of General Treatment Strategies Accounting for Time-Varying Covariates
literature.what_it_means: Waymark's interest in observational causal methods makes this unreviewed preprint potentially relevant. It proposes estimating heterogeneous effects with time-varying covariates under conditional parallel trends assumptions. It could inform program evaluation where treatment and covariates change over time, but has not been validated in Waymark data.

literature.title: SurvICL: a Foundation Model for in-context Survival Analysis
literature.what_it_means: SurvICL could inform whom to reach through risk prediction. This methods preprint reports synthetic pretraining and strong held-out survival benchmark performance, not demonstrated benefits for outreach. Transfer to Medicaid remains unestablished.

literature.title: Artificial Intelligence in Health Insurance: An Interagency Framework for Federal and State Oversight
literature.venue: The Journal of law, medicine & ethics : a journal of the American Society of Law, Medicine & Ethics
literature.what_it_means: Policy framework paper on AI governance in insurance, not empirical evidence. Relevant to Waymark's AI deployment and safety concerns, but no data on impact, validation, or operationalization in Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Community Health Worker Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review
literature.venue: Applied health economics and health policy
literature.what_it_means: This review is relevant to Waymark's CHW program: included studies focused on adults with type 2 diabetes from low-income and/or ethnic minority populations. Heterogeneous designs limit interpretation. The abstract does not specify study countries or report Medicaid-specific findings, so applicability to US Medicaid managed care needs assessment.

literature.title: Prevalent knowledge omissions: An unseen risk of LLMs in patient-friendly adaptation of medical literature
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's LLM safety concerns (Anchor product, COMPASS). However, uses a dataset of chemical-disease relations, not clinical notes or member-facing text. Transfer to Waymark's actual adaptation workflows requires validation.

literature.title: Dynamic pathways of maternal well-being: A longitudinal latent class analysis of risk and adaptive trajectories in low-income families
literature.what_it_means: Study identifies maternal mental health subgroups and trajectories in low-income populations similar to Waymark's demographic. Findings could inform behavioral health targeting and social needs screening, but lacks intervention component and does not address Medicaid-managed-care care-team workflow.

literature.title: County-Level Context and Differential Policy Impacts on Buprenorphine Use Among Medicaid Enrollees with Opioid Use Disorder in Kentucky, 2018–2025
literature.what_it_means: Interrupted time series of policy changes affecting medication access and use in Medicaid OUD population. Relevant to care coordination outreach and pharmacist medication review, but unclear if findings would inform Waymark's reach, team actions, or product behavior without adaptation.

literature.title: Applications of Transformer-Based pretrained language models for analyzing nursing records in adult Care: A scoping review
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of transformer-based models for adult nursing notes. Relevant to Waymark's care-note analysis and LLM safety work, but Medicaid applicability is unclear. One study reported prospective silent evaluation; none evaluated clinical deployment or effects on clinical outcomes.

literature.title: Social Risk Screening and Referrals in the Pediatric Inpatient Setting
literature.what_it_means: Describes screening prevalence and practices but no causal evidence on impact. Inpatient acute setting differs from Waymark's community-based outpatient model. No health outcomes or cost data.

literature.title: Large Language Models in the Emergency Department: Fairness Implications for Clinicians
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM fairness risks relevant to Waymark's AI products (Signal, Compass, Anchor). The framework may inform Medicaid applications, but this emergency-care narrative review does not establish specific harms, effective solutions, or transferability.

literature.title: Explainable AI in Healthcare: A Holistic View of Technical Approaches, Regulatory Frameworks, Reliable Clinical Implementation Insights and Limitations
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Anchor's verification layer and Waymark's LLM safety interests. Reviews XAI techniques for identifying bias and analyzing hallucinations, but does not establish their usefulness for omission-error evaluation. Limited actionable guidance for Medicaid care-team workflows.

literature.title: Internal Consistency Does Not Validate an LLM-Assisted Nutrition Pipeline: A Reference-Standard-Free Forensic Reliability Audit of 13,073 Free-Text Meal Records
literature.what_it_means: The audit suggests reproducibility checks and intermediate-output inspection that may inform Anchor's verification work. It does not directly evaluate omission detection or Signal's risk predictions. Transfer from nutrition logging in rural Colombia to Medicaid care coordination needs explicit justification.

literature.title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
literature.what_it_means: Foundation model for risk prediction could improve Signal's rising-risk detection, but evidence is from a single hospital's insured population, not Medicaid managed care. No prospective validation or operational deployment shown.

literature.title: Postpartum Medicaid extensions and follow-up care after pregnancy complications
literature.what_it_means: Studies postpartum Medicaid population Waymark serves but focuses narrowly on insurance continuity effect on utilization. Does not directly inform whom to reach, care-team actions, or product behavior without further analysis.

literature.title: Estimation of Area Deprivation Index Rankings in South Dakota Using Spatiotemporal Change of Support Method
literature.what_it_means: Addresses geographic misalignment in SDOH measurement, relevant to targeting. This South Dakota methods study's abstract reports no health-outcome evaluation or Medicaid-setting validation; integration into Waymark operations remains unclear.

literature.title: Telepharmacological Consultation for Polypharmacy Management in Primary Care: A Qualitative Study of General Practitioners' Experiences With Cross‐Sectoral Coordination
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study of pharmacist–GP coordination for polypharmacy in Danish primary care. Addresses pharmacy program workflow integration and care-coordination gaps. Setting differs (single-payer, hospital-based service vs. Medicaid managed care). Small sample limits generalizability.

literature.title: Cognition, oversight, and the safety case for documentation AI
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's verification layer and LLM-safety interests. Hospital discharge setting differs from Waymark's community-based Medicaid care. Mechanism (oversight attenuation) plausibly transfers; population does not.

literature.title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts
literature.what_it_means: Unreviewed preprint evaluated on 36 EHR benchmark tasks, not members or claims data. It targets temporal and index-date errors that matter given Waymark's claims lag and staggered ADT start dates. It does not show that the resulting effect estimates are valid or survive falsification.

literature.title: Learning Who Benefits Most: Multi-Treatment Causal Ranking for Population Health Stratification
literature.what_it_means: Unreviewed preprint tested only on synthetic and semi-synthetic data from the Italian system. Waymark's per-member treatment-effect rankings did not validate out of sample, and recovering generated orderings does not address that failure. Revisit if a real-outcome validation appears.

literature.title: Seeded Probes Do Not Identify a Reviewer's Miss Rate: One-Sided Misclassification in Distribution-Free Risk Control
literature.what_it_means: Anchor and Compass safety rest on physician review of AI outputs. The paper argues that planted-error probes cannot validate those reviewers. Physician miss rates varied widely. The argument is mainly formal and fits any setting, but this is an unreviewed preprint with simulations and a small empirical sample of 17 physicians.

literature.title: Adjudicator sensitivity of safety estimates in large language models for open-ended cardiovascular reasoning: a blinded multi-adjudicator benchmark study running title: adjudicator variability in LLM safety
literature.what_it_means: This is a peer-reviewed methods study. One adjudicator flagged 17.7% of responses as unsafe and the other flagged 0%. Single-reviewer safety audits like this bear directly on how Waymark validates Anchor and Compass outputs. The domain is cardiology, not Medicaid, but the measurement problem transfers.

literature.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Linking Medicaid and Education Records in New York City
literature.venue: International Journal for Population Data Science
literature.what_it_means: Peer-reviewed methods work linking children's Medicaid and education records. It may inform linkage of messy administrative sources such as claims, ADT and CBO referrals. The abstract reports linkage coverage, not a validated accuracy estimate, and reports no health outcomes. Its operational value for Waymark remains to be assessed.

literature.title: Factors Associated with Early ED Return Among Patients Discharged After Treatment for Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome
literature.what_it_means: Single-site retrospective review with only 14 returns within 72 hours and wide confidence intervals. Covariates were selected by univariate screening. Schizophrenia, anxiety and Medicaid coverage were associated with 72-hour return; homelessness with 30-day admission. Relevant to post-ED outreach, but larger studies are needed before using these findings to guide targeting.

literature.title: “I don't have to choose between everything”: Self-reported fruit and vegetable affordability, purchasing shifts, and healthcare utilization among produce prescription program participants in North Carolina
literature.what_it_means: Produce prescriptions may be relevant to Medicaid social-needs work, but this uncontrolled online survey relies on recalled before/after affordability and self-reported healthcare use. It cannot establish that the programs caused improvements. No claims-based outcomes are reported. Worth tracking alongside controlled produce-prescription evaluations.

literature.title: Assessing the ability of cross-trained pharmacy technician-community health workers to identify non-medical drivers of health resources
literature.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
literature.what_it_means: Descriptive analysis of training assignments, not patient encounters. It reports no referral completion, no member outcomes and no Medicaid-specific population. Cross-training pharmacy staff as CHWs is conceptually relevant to Waymark's team mix, but nothing here would change practice or evaluation yet.

literature.title: Embedded Psychological Services and Lower 60-Day Acute-Care Utilization in High-Need, High-Cost Adults: A Target Trial Emulation
literature.venue: The journal of behavioral health services & research
literature.what_it_means: These high-need safety-net adults may resemble some Waymark members. Comparing engagers with decliners/no-shows risks unmeasured selection bias despite weighting. The E-value of 2.37 does not establish whether motivation explains the association. Admissions were not statistically significant. The design differs from Waymark's lesson favoring quasi-random operational variation.

literature.title: A University and Community Partnership to Address Diaper Insecurity Among Infants in Suburban Communities Through Home Visiting Services
literature.venue: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
literature.what_it_means: The population and the CHW home-visit model closely match Waymark's pediatric Medicaid work. But this is a descriptive, post-only survey of 88 respondents with self-reported outcomes and no comparison group. It shows feasibility, not effect, so it is not enough to change practice yet.

literature.title: Federal Immigration Enforcement Deployment and Emergency Department Utilization Among Children
literature.what_it_means: This single-site study may inform Waymark's equity and evaluation work, but Medicaid coverage was not reported. Over a short window, it measured visits, not individual children. The reported counts cannot distinguish care avoidance from shifts to other sites. It flags a potential access concern, not a validated intervention.

literature.title: Patient Navigation Plus mHealth Incentives for Linkage to OUD Care for Adults Who Also Use Methamphetamines
literature.what_it_means: Small single-site pilot RCT in hospitalized Washington adults with OUD and methamphetamine use who started buprenorphine. At 30 days, linkage was 55% vs 50% (risk ratio 1.10; wide CI crossing 1), so effectiveness remains uncertain. Feasibility and navigation satisfaction were encouraging; applicability to Waymark's broader Medicaid population needs assessment.

literature.title: Protocol for the Nutrition OUtReach In Systems of Healthcare (NOURISH) trial: a phase II multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial of medically tailored groceries to prevent malnutrition in transplant and cellular therapy patients
literature.what_it_means: It reports no outcomes. The population is a narrow, high-acuity oncology transplant group in specialty centers, and payer mix is unreported. The planned sample is modest, and the primary endpoint is clinical malnutrition rather than utilization. Results could still inform food-as-medicine referral design.

literature.title: Low‐Intensity Social Care for Dementia Caregivers: A Randomized Trial
literature.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
literature.what_it_means: Peer-reviewed RCT with a null primary outcome. Lower self-reported ED use was a secondary finding with a wide CI among caregivers with social risks; no ED difference was detected without social risks. Participants were mostly Black and urban, with mixed incomes, and were not Medicaid-specific. Transfer to Waymark is uncertain. Text-navigator uptake was high.

literature.title: Impact of a National Stepped‐Care Model of Opioid Use Disorder Treatment on Access to Medication Therapies Among Homeless‐Experienced Veterans
literature.what_it_means: Facility-level train-the-trainer support for stepped-care opioid use disorder treatment outside specialty settings was associated with higher buprenorphine receipt among homeless-experienced veterans, with no significant differences in methadone or naltrexone receipt.

literature.title: Self-Adjusting Long-Term Medications: A Qualitative Descriptive Study of Patients’ Practices
literature.what_it_means: Small descriptive interview study. Country, payer and patient characteristics are not reported, so transfer to Medicaid members is unclear. It describes reasons for self-adjustment but tests no intervention. The themes may inform how pharmacists frame medication reviews, but it is not enough to change practice.

literature.title: Woebot for Postpartum Mood and Anxiety: Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of a Mobile Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Intervention
literature.what_it_means: Pilot RCT with a waitlist control and self-reported outcomes. The efficacy signal is weak (d=-0.16, n=97 symptomatic), and the improvement in stress was exploratory. The sample was mostly White, recruited through a research platform, and payer was not reported, so the Medicaid postpartum transfer is unproven. Engagement was modest, a median of 9 days.
